title: Send email
description: Send an email through Amazon SES.
$sideEffectsComment: SES has no idempotency header, so a retry sends a second email. Resend declares `idempotent` because it accepts a key and the generated executor supplies one; there is nothing equivalent here, so this is the honest answer rather than the matching one.

requireOneOf.error: needs a "text" or "html" body — SES refuses a Content.Simple with neither, and an empty email is never intended

config.label: From
config.description: Must be a VERIFIED identity in this region. An address verified in another region does not exist here.

config.label: To
config.description: One address, a comma-separated list, or an expression. While the account is in the SES sandbox, anything not verified is accepted by the API and silently never delivered.

config.label: Configuration set
config.description: Optional. SES routes engagement events (bounces, complaints, opens) through the set you name.

outputShape.description: Which estate this ran against. SES has no separate one, so: fake or live.
The connection id that was used.
SES's id for the send. It means ACCEPTED, not delivered — and in the sandbox an unverified recipient is accepted and discarded.
